chapter: Louis Dumaine and Kid Rene bands
title: Pay disputes and Gabriel's large family
summary: George Lewis's wife signs contracts and pays the men; Rene is always owing. Gabriel notes his eleven children and puts his brother August in the band.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: So George played every job Rene played. His wife would only have $6 for Rene, $1 for the leader, $5 for the men. That's where when he got $6 we got $5. His wife would sign the contract and Rene didn't get none of that money. So when he played he had to owe George Lewis $2. He owed the time one player $2. That's where Morris French put the band. He owed him a long time. His brother owed $2-$3. He owed a dollar. Son Thomas. Always in trouble but he couldn't owe me nothing because I had too many children.

At 16 I got 11 living. So we played together. Later on then the job kind of came out and we went and played down by the alley. I put my brother in the band August too. I got August in that band with a given name. I know we played up there. So later on we pulled around and see what we did that job. That's right. We got out the band, me and August. So they went playing down by the alley. I wonder if you could tell me some more about that alley because that's right next to the St. Bernard market. Yeah. Well I didn't play down there but Rene took the job and he enjoyed it.
